summary: New box Infectum: example for sense 1 in Infectum (Jan 2.35/5650)

data.turoyo: I naqqa d əzzanowo lə qriṯo, i qriṯo kula, ləḏʕatwo man gədmadlox lu baytayḏe! Man gədmaʕbarlox w man gədḥuḏanlox!
data.translation: When we used to go to a village, the whole village, you would not know who would take you to his house, who would bring you in and who would embrace you!

rationale: First Infectum box absent after round 1; prospective gədḥuḏanlox with overt hospitality context. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation; the sense is based on the Turoyo.

data.turoyo: Mədlele lu Sarkosa. Lə qadər d maqəmle mu aḥuno. Mədlele lu naʕimo, ḥḏəlle qum ṣadre, maqəmle mu aḥuno.
data.translation: Sarkosa fasste ihn, aber er vermochte nicht, ihn von seinem Bruder in die Höhe zu heben. Da fasste der jüngste ihn, schlang seine Arme um seine Brust und befreite so seinen Bruder von ihm.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell; hostile wrestling clasp extends the same arms-around action beyond greeting.

data.turoyo: Ǧafəl w ʕayne rawiḥi: "Ḥurma, mə kit?" — "Lo zayʕat!" Azza, ftəḥla u tarʕo w aṯyo, msəkla, ḥḏ̣əlla hawxa.
data.translation: Er fuhr zusammen und riß die Augen weit auf. "Frau, was ist los?" "So hab doch keine Angst!" Sie ging und machte die Türe auf, hielt ihn aber dabei fest, und schlang die Arme um ihn.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell; female actor holds and embraces a frightened husband.

data.turoyo: Li ḥurma məllale lu aḥunayḏa: “Qum! Aḥuno, nfaq larwal!” Nafəq larwal, me du sabʕo ḥzele u aḥunayḏa u naʕimo yo, fṣəḥ ebe fṣiḥuṯo rabṯo, mədle, ḥḏ̣əlle w nšəqle, məlle: “ʕAl ʕayni w d babi aṯət ġalabe!”
data.translation: Da sprach die Frau zu ihrem Bruder: "Los, Bruder, komm heraus! "Er kam heraus, und als der Löwe sah, daß es der jüngste war, freute er sich sehr über ihn, umarmte ihn und küßte ihn, und sprach: "Du bist hochwillkommen, auf meine und meines Vaters Augen!"

rationale: Thin Preterit cell; the lion’s greeting offers a full affective context.

data.turoyo: Qayimo w ḥḏ̣əlla w nšəqla u aḥuno d ruḥa, ḥḏ̣əlla.
data.translation: Sie umarmte Ihren Bruder und küßte ihn und Schloss ihn in die Arme.

rationale: Fifth distinct Preterit example including the inherited one; female actor and overt brother, with repeated embracing around kissing.

data.turoyo: Naḥət l qamuṯayna, qamayto aṯi ḥḏənlelan. W ḥḏənlan ḥḏoḏe, xəd i ʕade. Bəṯər u qašo, bəṯər i ǧamaʕa, ḥḏənile hanək stene.
data.translation: He came down to meet us. First he came and embraced us. And we embraced one another, as is customary. Then the priest, then the congregation; I embraced those too.

rationale: Unusual retained-n forms contrast 3sg agent plus 1pl patient, reciprocal 1pl agent and uncertain -ile. One context for three occurrences, beyond the filled cell only for form/valency evidence. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation; the sense is based on the Turoyo.

summary: The Preterit -le/-la agent forms show root-final n assimilated to l; the plain ḏ of PrS 41/52 is copied unchanged rather than normalized to ḏ̣.
Objects are bare NPs or recoverable people; qum ṣadre supplies the chest relation in the wrestling context.
The repeated ḥḏ̣əlla at 61/208 emphasizes the welcome around a kissing predicate. It is two occurrences but one example, so it does not inflate cell counts.
All six analyses support stem I Preterit sense 1. There are no proposed new senses or new boxes.
Jan has undotted ḥḏən- with retained n before suffixes, contrasting with glossary ḥḏ̣əlle. These spellings are preserved as evidence, not treated as a separate root or stem.
Object suffixes -li and -lan contrast with l-agent suffixes. The reciprocal object ḥḏoḏe does not license a Detransitive label.

Preterit has five examples after round 1; only a compact unusual-form/reciprocity context is added. The first Infectum is selected. The Arabic quotation in 3874 is contextual speech and contributes no Turoyo verb-form evidence.
PrS 41/52: does qum ṣadre mean against the youngest brother’s chest, or around Bardawil’s chest? The possessive reference is not settled by the German alone.

Jan 2.12/2931: segment ḥḏənile; does -ile encode a first-person agent with plural patient, or another agent/patient pattern? The embracing meaning is secure, exact suffix analysis remains provisional.
Jan 2.35/5650: confirm ḥuḏan- vocalism against glossary ḥoḏ̣ən; preserve source spelling until native review.
A hostile restraining clasp in PrS 41/52 retains the physical arms-around meaning of umarmen; hostile purpose does not justify a second sense.
Hostile grappling in Jan 1.8/186 supports the round-1 restraint extension, without a second sense. Reciprocal embracing is expressed by ḥḏoḏe with the ordinary active Preterit.
